messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure which one will give first. The regime’s still standing, but the pieces aren’t fitting together like they used to, and the quiet out there? That’s not calm. It’s the kind of quiet before something shifts."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime’s not just digging in; it’s building for the long haul. People are still whispering, but the whispers aren’t turning into shouts. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a storm—yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The machine is running smoother than it should—too smooth, like they’re trying to prove nothing’s wrong. But the cracks are there: the retraction in the paper, the money moving, even the shopkeeper saying what he said. No one’s moving yet, but the air feels like it’s holding its breath—waiting for someone to blink first."*"
Sender 4: "*"Something’s shifting under the surface—no big moves yet, but the cracks are showing. The regime’s still standing, but the pieces aren’t fitting like they used to. Keep your eyes open, but don’t make any sudden moves. We’ll know more soon."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—but they’re not shaking. The elites are settling scores fast, the borders are quiet, and even the World Bank is nodding along. People are talking, but only in whispers with one foot out the door. The regime’s not collapsing… but it’s not sleeping either. We should assume it’s stronger than it looks—at least for now."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like they’ve got the reins tighter than ever—no cracks, no leaks, just business as usual, even when things *should* be messy. The only question now is whether anyone’s left with the stomach to try and shake it."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundations aren’t shaking—yet. The generals aren’t packing their bags, the banks aren’t panicking, and the kids in the streets are just repeating what their parents mutter at night. But those half-sentences? They’re adding up. The real question isn’t if the regime cracks—it’s how long it can keep pretending the cracks aren’t there."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s tighter than ever, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: the censors are slipping, the streets are tired, not angry, and the elites are acting like they’ve already won. That’s either confidence or desperation, but either way, we’re not seeing the real fight yet—if there even is one. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a collapse. Not yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are listening harder than ever—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans now—but the machine’s still humming along like nothing’s wrong. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, it’s whether we’ll see the cracks before they see us."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re holding together for now—tighter than we thought, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The real question isn’t whether they’ll fall, but whether anyone’s left who actually wants to push them."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the signs are clear—they’re not just holding on, they’re digging in deeper. The promotions, the spending, even the way people grumble like it’s just background noise… it’s not fear, it’s resignation. And that’s the scariest part."*"
Sender 12: "*"The cracks are there—patronage is unraveling, and even the loyalists are feeling the squeeze—but no one’s ready to move yet. The streets are quiet, the security forces are still in line, and the money’s holding… for now. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether anyone will see it coming in time to act—or if we’ll all just keep waiting until it’s too late."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. No cracks in the foundation, no panic in the ranks, just the usual quiet nods between us. The regime’s not just standing; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the streets are humming along like nothing’s wrong. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it’s business as usual—just with a little more caution than usual."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the machine is still running smoothly—no cracks in the command chain, and the money’s flowing like always. But something’s off: the graffiti stayed up too long, the clinic’s stocking up, and the top brass is repeating the same lines like they’re trying to convince themselves. Stability for now, but don’t get comfortable—if things shift, it’ll happen fast."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the surface is calm—too calm, maybe. The machine is running, but the gears are grinding just a little too loud. Payments are late, the streets are quiet but restless, and the diplomats are asking questions they shouldn’t have to. If something shifts—even a nudge—this could go either way fast. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet. We’re not out of the woods, just stuck in the thick of them."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re holding things together—for now—but it’s like watching someone juggle while the floor is slowly giving out. The shops are busy, the security’s out there, and the bigwigs are still playing their games, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. My bet? They’re buying time, not winning it. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like they’ve got the upper hand for now—checkpoints thinning, businesses hiring, even that old rival singing their praises. But the real tell? People are talking *just* a little louder, like they’re testing the air. Still, no one’s dumb enough to push too far—yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet on anything breaking soon."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the cracks are there—people are whispering, the shopkeeper even said it out loud—but the walls aren’t shaking. The inner circle’s locking arms tighter, the security forces are still marching in step, and the money’s still flowing (just in dollars now, which says something). No one’s packing bags yet, just booking vacations like nothing’s wrong. They’re not scared enough to run, just nervous enough to hedge. We’re in the long game here—no quick collapse, but no iron grip either. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your ears open for the things they’re *not* saying."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are circling the wagons tighter, security’s getting sharper, and even the clinic’s stocking up like they’re expecting a storm. People are talking, but only in whispers, and the regime’s making sure nothing slips through. The real question is how long they can keep this up if the economy starts to crack."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no panic. But the regime’s starting to sweat a little: they’re moving things around behind the scenes, keeping the security forces sharp, and even throwing a few bones to the usual suspects. The streets are quiet, but the censorship’s slipping—like they’re not even trying as hard to hide the rot. For now, they’ve got the upper hand, but if the pressure keeps building, even the strongest dam can give way. Stay sharp, stay low, and keep your ears open."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re holding on, but it’s getting harder—like a dam with cracks you can’t see yet. The old networks are stirring, the security forces are restless, and the bureaucracy is slowing down. The question isn’t if something breaks, but what happens when the regime realizes it’s not as strong as it thinks."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where you can hear the ice cracking underfoot—just not where you’re standing yet. The regime’s tightening its grip in some places while quietly pulling back in others, and the streets? Too quiet. Not calm, just waiting. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re holding the line for now—no cracks in the walls, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot. The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel, and the passengers? They’re starting to hum a different tune."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re holding it together for now—too well, honestly. The cracks are there, but they’re papered over with discipline and cash, and the kids in the streets are singing what their parents taught them. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but how long they can keep pretending it won’t."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the surface is calm, but something’s shifting under it—elites are locked in, the military’s not on edge, and even the jokes are getting bolder. The regime’s either too confident or too distracted to care, but the smart money’s already moving. Stay sharp—this could be the quiet before something, or just the quiet before nothing. Either way, don’t assume we’re seeing the whole picture."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
